summary: Spike of client retry surge masked as slow inference — 429s interpreted as timeouts for AtlasAnalytics
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden increase in end-to-end tail latency for calls to the /v1/chat/stream endpoint. AtlasAnalytics observed many user transactions that appear to stall for tens of seconds and then fail. Impact: batch of customer endpoints saw 10-20x increase in perceived latency and an increase in error rate from 0.2% to 8% over a 2 hour window. Environment: prod | us-east | Dedicated pool A. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use AtlasAnalytics SDK configuration (default retries=3, backoff=100ms). 2) Simulate 120 TPS with concurrency of 100 across multiple clients using same API key. 3) Observe some streams stall and many requests receive 429, client immediately retries and aggregates latency. Observed behaviour: high rate of 429 responses interleaved with slow streaming; many client retries cause connection churn and aggregated queueing at API gateway, producing long tail latency and occasional 504 timeouts. Expected behaviour: 429s surface as explicit rate-limit responses with Retry-After headers, SDK honor Retry-After/backoff and avoid immediate retries so overall system latency remains stable. Logs and traces: api-gateway logs show per-key spike in requests at 2026-02-27T18:12Z; rate-limiter counters report exhausted token buckets; serving-runtime traces show many short-lived connections and repeated auth checks.
comments: 2026-02-28 Priya Kapoor: Customer opened after noticing a latency spike coinciding with a marketing rollout. Customer says their SDKs are default settings and they saw retries happen within 200ms of 429s.
2026-03-01 Daniel Cho: Investigating. Asked for customer SDK config and representative request IDs. Provided: req ids: rq_ae12.., rq_ae19..; asked customer to run capture with --dump-headers.

2026-03-01 AtlasAnalytics (Customer): Uploaded representative capture and stated they could reproduce by running a smoke test at 80-120 TPS. Confirmed SDK version 0.9.4 and default client retry/backoff settings.

2026-03-02 SRE (Marta Ruiz): Found adapter logs showing retries honoring SDK backoff but Retry-After was absent in some 429 responses due to soft-quota enforcement path. Filed INT-4543 for rate-limiter behaviour in soft-quota mode.

2026-03-03 Daniel Cho: Temporarily increased soft-quota window for AtlasAnalytics for 2 hours to reduce immediate 429 occurrence while fix is deployed. Customer confirmed improved latency during that window.
2026-03-04 Priya Kapoor: Closing ticket after validation and documentation updates. Customer accepted recommended SDK config changes.
2026-03-04 AtlasAnalytics (Customer): Confirmed they will upgrade SDK and add exponential backoff in their integration. Thanks for quick turnaround.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: SDK immediate retry behaviour amplifies a transient quota enforcement signal (soft-quota 429s) into a larger traffic surge, creating queueing at API gateway.
Hypothesis 2: Some 429s from the soft-quota path were missing Retry-After header; SDKs that rely on Retry-After did not implement additional exponential backoff, causing fast retries.

Evidence: Grafana panels (requests/sec, 5xx, 429) show tight correlation between sudden drop in X-RateLimit-Remaining and burst of retries for single API key at 2026-02-27T18:12Z. Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/alerts/atlas-reqs?orgId=1&from=1614550000000&to=1614557200000

Logs: api-gateway access logs contain repeated entries from same source IP within <150ms intervals for same request id prefix. Rate-limiter logs show token-bucket drains to 0 for the tenant and soft-quota enforcement path returned plain 429 without Retry-After in ~37% of samples.
Reproducer notes: Running the customer's smoke test with SDK 0.9.4 and forced Retry-After absence reproduced the tail latency and 504s locally against staging gateway.

Findings: Primary contributor is client-side retry amplification combined with soft-quota 429 responses lacking Retry-After headers. Secondary contributor: dedicated pool autoscaler had a cooldown which delayed capacity increase under sudden retry surge.
Related work: INT-4543 tracks fixing soft-quota 429 header omission; infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4582 addresses header consistency and smoothing token-bucket refill rate.
resolution: Workaround applied: Temporarily increased customer's soft quota and smoothing window from 50rps->120rps for 2 hours to allow backlog to drain. Customer reported immediate improvement.

Customer guidance: Instructed AtlasAnalytics to upgrade SDK to 0.10.1+ which implements exponential backoff and respects Retry-After. Recommended SDK config: max_retries=2, base_backoff_ms=500, max_backoff_ms=5000.

Platform fixes: Deployed infra PR #4582 to ensure 429 responses from soft-quota path include Retry-After and to add small randomized jitter to token-bucket refill for dedicated pools to reduce lockstep retries.
Autoscaler change: Shortened autoscaler cooldown for dedicated pools during quota-exhaustion events and added alert rule for rapid per-key retry spikes.
Follow-ups: INT-4543 assigned to infra team for longer-term rate-limiter smoothing; added a console dashboard tile to surface per-key 429 and retry amplification incidents to CS and SRE.
Status: Customer validated fix in prod flags and agreed to delay marketing rollout for 48h to monitor stability. Ticket closed after 48h observation window with no recurrence.
